about: The statement of how far each Series read from its Origin may be from v1's over the Periods both hold, and why: M13's for BLS, Treasury Fiscal Data and the Federal Reserve Board, and M16's for the rest of v1's series that are live (the IMF's, the BEA's, the EIA's and the Census Bureau's). scripts/v1-overlap.mjs compares a release built from a capture store with a release of v1's values (atlas legacy-release) against it. abs is in v1's unit: half a unit of the last decimal v1 kept (two for a figure in percent, three otherwise) unless why says more; rel is a share of v1's figure. factor brings the Origin's unit to v1's. exceptions are Periods further off than the tolerance, each with what was found; they are counted, never hidden. different marks a Series that is another quantity than v1's by a recorded decision. v1: null says v1 had no such Series. A Period the engine marks partial (the month in progress) is not compared. The comparison is of figures fetched within days of each other: an Origin's later revision is a difference this file does not allow for. Nothing here is data.

v1 held the quarter-end total in millions of dollars from FRED's GFDEBTN; here the last business day of the quarter from Debt to the Penny, in dollars, is divided by a million. FRED's figures are whole millions and come from another Treasury publication. 93 of the 106 quarters agree to within $1 million and six more to within $3.6 million; $5 million (under a millionth of the total) is allowed, and the seven quarters beyond it are explained one by one.

exceptions.2020-Q1: v1's figure is the total of 31 January 2020 (to $0.12 million), not of 31 March: about $463 billion less than the quarter's end.
exceptions.2013-Q4: v1's figure is the total of 31 October 2013 (to $1.9 million), not of 31 December: about $196 billion less than the quarter's end.
exceptions.2012-Q1: v1's figure is $24.4 billion (0.16 percent) above Debt to the Penny for 30 March 2012 and matches no day near it. Not traced further.
exceptions.2010-Q2: v1's figure is $1.7 billion (0.013 percent) below Debt to the Penny for 30 June 2010. Not traced further.
exceptions.2012-Q2: v1's figure is $1.3 billion (0.008 percent) below Debt to the Penny for 29 June 2012. Not traced further.
exceptions.2003-Q3: v1's figure is $89 million above Debt to the Penny for 30 September 2003. Not traced further.
exceptions.2005-Q4: v1's figure is $11.5 million below Debt to the Penny for 30 December 2005. Not traced further.

The engine's own monthly mean differs from v1's in a month whose last Wednesday's week ends in the next month: a difference of representation, stated in docs/v2/v1-overlap.md.

The same index on another base: v1's (the OECD's, through FRED, ending June 2021) is on 2015 = 100 and the Fund's on 2020 = 100. Each is printed to one decimal on its own base, so their ratio is not one number: over the 258 months both hold it runs from 1.0173 to 1.0186. The Fund's figure is multiplied by 1.018 and may then be 0.08 of an index point (under a tenth of a percent) from v1's.

The same index on another base: v1's (the OECD's) is on 2015 = 100 and the Fund's on 2020 = 100. v1's figure is 1.1155 times the Fund's throughout; after that factor the two are within 0.005 of an index point, which is the rounding of the factor.

The month's average rate from another compiler: v1 read the OECD's figure through FRED and this is the Fund's. In 95 percent of the 321 months the two are within half a percent of each other; in months of sharp moves (2006, 2018, 2021, 2023) they are up to 3.5 percent apart, which is what two averages of one month's daily rates can differ by when the rate moves by a tenth within it. 3.5 percent of v1's figure is allowed.

The twelve-month change of an index printed to one decimal, on two bases (jp_cpi). A rounding of 0.05 of an index point at each end of a year moves the change by up to a tenth of a percentage point; 0.14 is the most the two differ by in the 258 months both hold.

v1 kept two decimals of a figure in percent, computed from the index on its 2015 base; here it is computed from the index on the Fund's base (cn_cpi). One month in 322 is 0.00501 away, a hair over half a unit of v1's last decimal.

v1 took the monthly balance from FRED (BOPGSTB); here it is the Census Bureau's own flat file of the FT-900 release, in whole millions of dollars. 259 of the 321 months are equal. In 50 months, all before 2017, the two differ by exactly $1 million: the balance is the difference of exports and imports, each rounded to a million, and can be rounded once or twice. $1 million is allowed. The twelve months of 2000 are further apart and are explained by name.

exceptions.2000-01: One of the twelve months of 2000, in which the two differ by $143 million to $1.16 billion (at most 4 percent of the month's balance) and by $4 million over the year: the year's total is the same and its division among the months is not, as after a revision of seasonal factors that one of the two carries and the other does not. Not traced further.
